skill.name: browser-devtools
skill.description: Inspect and debug Chrome web apps with the native agent-browser CLI and Chrome DevTools. Use for network requests, console errors, source debugging, storage, performance/CPU/memory analysis, React component trees and render profiling, and browser-driven reproduction. Start with a compact overview, then inspect relevant details using installed APIs.

content.user_title: Debug Chrome Web Apps with DevTools
content.value_statement: Chrome web problems often require evidence from several browser surfaces, which makes diagnosis slow and inconsistent. This skill provides a focused workflow for reproducing issues, collecting bounded evidence, and verifying fixes with agent-browser and Chrome DevTools.
actual_capabilities: Reproduce Chrome web app issues with a persistent, isolated browser session.
Inspect requests, redirects, cookies, storage, service workers, and cache behavior.
Investigate console errors, source maps, breakpoints, DOM, CSS, workers, and accessibility state.
Capture focused performance traces, CPU evidence, heap behavior, and memory retention clues.
Inspect React component branches, props, state, hooks, rerenders, and commit profiles when supported.
Explain observed evidence, likely causes, controlled experiments, and verified results.
limitations: It cannot prove production performance or real-user Core Web Vitals from a single local trace.
React inspection depends on page registration, compatible builds, and available DevTools support.
It does not replace functional tests, deployment checks, or backend observability.
Browser scripts can have application side effects, so authorized disposable environments are required for mutations.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a failed API request
use_cases.description: Capture the failing transaction, inspect redirects and browser policies, trace the initiator, and verify the repair under comparable conditions.

use_cases.title: Find a slow interaction
use_cases.description: Record a focused interaction, separate network, rendering, and JavaScript costs, then identify the dominant measured path.

use_cases.title: Investigate a React rendering issue
use_cases.description: Inspect the relevant component branch and profile repeated commits without dumping unrelated application state.

prompt_templates.title: Start a browser diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this Chrome issue: [describe the symptom]. Use the intended test URL, reproduce it once, and report the observed evidence, likely cause, and next check.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a failed request
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the failed request for [action]. Capture the request and response details, redirect or preflight behavior, initiating source, and resulting UI state. Redact secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a slow interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile [interaction] in an isolated session. Record a short comparable trace, separate network, scripting, rendering, and paint costs, and identify the dominant measured path.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a React performance hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate whether [component or interaction] causes repeated expensive renders. Inspect the smallest relevant React branch, profile the same interaction before and after one controlled change, and report limits.

output_examples.input: The checkout button appears to do nothing after a recent frontend change.
output_examples.output: Evidence: the click reaches the page, but the request is blocked during preflight. Cause: the new origin is missing the required CORS response. Verification: the same authorized test action succeeds after the server policy is corrected.

output_examples.input: A dashboard becomes slow after switching between two filters.
output: Trace result: repeated rendering dominates the measured interaction.
Relevant path: the filter change remounts the results branch and repeats expensive work.
Next check: compare an equivalent interaction after stabilizing the branch identity.

output_examples.input: A React panel rerenders whenever an unrelated control changes.
output_examples.output: The focused component branch receives a changed object identity from its parent. The profile shows extra commits, but it does not establish a production-wide performance impact.

best_practices: Start collection before reproduction and keep the investigation scoped to the failing origin and action.
Redact credentials, cookies, signed URLs, and sensitive payloads before sharing traces, screenshots, HARs, or heap data.
Change one condition at a time, preserve normal browser behavior, and repeat the same scenario after a fix.
anti_patterns: Do not replay requests, clear storage, change security settings, or mutate application state without authorization.
Do not dump whole globals, session objects, component trees, HAR files, or heap snapshots when bounded evidence is enough.
Do not treat one trace, a successful terminal request, or a mocked response as proof of production behavior.

faq.question: What browser does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Chrome through the native agent-browser CLI and Chrome DevTools workflows.

faq.question: Can it debug network and storage issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect requests, redirects, cookies, cache layers, service workers, and selected storage data.

faq.question: Can it measure real-world web performance?
faq.answer: No. Local traces help locate causes, but they do not establish field distributions or production Core Web Vitals.

faq.question: Does it support React applications?
faq.answer: Yes, when the page and build expose compatible React DevTools support. It also uses DOM and browser evidence when React access is unavailable.

faq.question: Is it safe to use on a logged-in browser?
faq.answer: Use an authorized session and prefer an isolated profile without restored authentication. Redact sensitive data from every shared artifact.

faq.question: Does it make code changes automatically?
faq.answer: It can investigate and validate requested fixes, but repository changes still require the project workflow and its required checks.
